content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines for the prevention and control of uterine cervical neoplasms, with a focus on the diagnosis and treatment of precancerous conditions. These guidelines are intended to provide evidence-based recommendations for healthcare professionals and policymakers to improve cervical cancer prevention strategies. The publication emphasizes that the designations and presentation of material do not imply any opinion from WHO regarding the legal status of any country, territory, or area, nor the delimitation of its boundaries. Any dotted lines on maps represent approximate borders where full agreement may not yet exist. Additionally, the mention of specific companies or products does not constitute endorsement or preference by WHO over others of a similar nature. WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information contained in the publication. However, the material is distributed without any warranty, expressed or implied. The responsibility for the interpretation and use of the material lies with the reader, and WHO shall not be held liable for any damages arising from its use. The guidelines include detailed recommendations for screening and treating precancerous cervical lesions to prevent cervical cancer. These strategies involve various screening methods, such as HPV testing, visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), cytology, and colposcopy, followed by treatment options like cryotherapy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). Specific algorithms are provided for different populations, including those with negative or unknown HIV status and those in areas with high endemic HIV infection. The development of these guidelines involved a comprehensive process, including the formation of a Guideline Development Group (GDG) and a Methods Group (MG). These groups collaborated to formulate PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) questions, evaluate evidence, and model health outcomes. The recommendations were reviewed and endorsed by an External Review Group (ERG). Conflicts of interest were managed through a transparent process. All experts involved were required to complete a WHO Declaration of Interest (DOI) form and disclose any relevant interests. These declarations were reviewed by WHO’s Office of the Legal Counsel, and all relevant interests were disclosed in the guidelines. The guidelines aim to enhance cervical cancer prevention by focusing on early detection and treatment of precancerous lesions. WHO acknowledges the contributions of the GDG, MG, and ERG, as well as the funding provided by organizations such as the Flanders International Cooperation Agency (FICA), Institut National du Cancer (INCa), and the GAVI Alliance. The document also includes annexes with detailed flowcharts for screening and treatment strategies, evidence review methodologies, and a list of studies included in the evidence reviews. Acronyms and abbreviations used throughout the guidelines are clearly defined for reference.
